references.text: The priest shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering to make atonement for the one who brings it.
The priest makes atonement for the person, and they receive forgiveness - the same theme of atonement (כִפֶּר) as in Leviticus 12:7.
The priest shall make atonement for the person, and their sin is forgiven - a parallel use of the concept of atonement.
The priest makes atonement for the one to be cleansed from their uncleanness - the same pattern of atonement and cleansing.
Cleansing from a discharge of blood in women - thematically parallel to cleansing from the flow of blood after childbirth.
Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the temple to fulfill the law of purification in Leviticus 12, and offer according to this regulation.
An alternative offering of two turtledoves or two young pigeons for one who cannot afford a lamb - the same offering regulation mentioned in Leviticus 12:8.
Earlier verses in the same chapter explaining the duration of uncleanness after the birth of a boy or a girl.
